sentences.text:
Papani Narender Goud , Naresh Goud vs The State Of A.P. on 20
July, 2023
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
Criminal Appeal Nos.208, 234 Of 2009 & 376 Of 2010
Common Judgment:

entities.text: Papani Narender Goud , Naresh Goud vs The State Of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1. Crl.A.No.376 of 2010 is preferred by A-1, Crl.A.No.234 of 2009 is preferred by A-2 and Crl.A.No.208 of 2009 is preferred by A-3.
2. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that victim/P.W.1, who was a minor on the date of incident was standing at Boath bus stand in order to go to her house.
A jeep came to the bus stand and in the said jeep A-1 to A-3 were seated.
They informed her that they were proceeding to Echoda Village.
After P.W.1 sat in the jeep, the accused took her in another route towards Sirikonda Village.
According to P.W.1, jeep was stopped, A-1 removed her pants and raped her.
Later, the accused went aside and while talking among themselves, P.W.1 escaped and hid in the bushes.
The next day morning, P.W.3 found P.W.1 in the bushes.
P.W.1 informed P.W.3 about the incident that happened on the earlier night.
P.W.3 provided a nighty and took her to the house and thereafter the incident was informed to her father/P.W.2.
P.W.2 filed a complaint/Ex.P.1.

During the course of investigation, on the basis of the complaint, the Police identified these appellants as perpetrators and accordingly, filed charge sheet for the offence under Section 376 of IPC against A-1 and Section 376 r/w 511 of IPC against A-2 and A-3.
The accused were also charged for the offence under Section 3 (i) (xi) and 3 (2) (v) of Schedule Castes/Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

3. Learned Sessions Judge having examined the victim/P.W.1 and other witnesses found A-1 guilty for the offence under Section 376 of IPC and A-2 and A-3 for the offence under Section 376 r/w 511 of IPC.
All the appellants were sentenced to 7 years of rigorous imprisonment.
No conviction was recorded under the provision of SC/ST (POA) Act.
4. Learned counsel appearing for A-1 would submit that there are any amount of discrepancies in the evidence of P.W.1, 2 and 3.
When the evidence is collectively read, no case is made out against any of the accused.
In fact, the very identification before the Court is doubtful, for the reason of there being no test identification parade during the course of investigation.

Admittedly, the accused are strangers to victim/P.W.1 and the entire incident happened in the night, the question of identifying the accused for the first time in the Court after three years is highly improbable.

5. On the other hand, learned Public Prosecutor would submit that though there are no specific allegations against A-2 and A-3, FSL report/EX.P.14 and the evidence of Doctor/P.W.15 would substantiate that it was A-1 who had committed rape on the victim/P.W.1.
The appeal of A-1 has to be dismissed.

sentences.text: 6. P.W.1 stated that while she was going to her village, these appellants have taken her in a jeep.
A-1 committed rape on her and there is no mention about A-2 and A-3 doing any acts except stating about their presence in the jeep.
After A-1 committed rape on P.W.1, according to her, when they were talking among themselves, she fled.
It is not the case that any of the accused chased her or tried to look for her in the bushes.
7. The wearing apparel of the victim/P.W.1 was seized and sent to DNA test.
The wearing apparel of the victim contained seminal stains which matched with the semen collected from A-1.

It was concluded in the FSL report that "the Autosomal STR analysis indicates that the seminal stains on source of item no.1 matches with DNA profile of source of item no.3 and conclusively proves that he is associated with the act."
There is no dispute regarding FSL report.
In the background of medical evidence collectively proving that A-1 was the person who had committed rape on P.W.1, the appeal of A-1 has to be dismissed.

8. Learned Sessions Judge found that during cross-examination of P.W.1 by the Public Prosecutor, it is stated by P.W.1 that she informed the Police that A-2 and A- 3 came towards her for committing rape and she put on her underwear and ran.
Though the victim stated that such a statement was made before the Police, she did not assert that the said statement made to the Police was correct regarding A-2 and A-3.
In the chief examination, she has not stated anything about A-2 and A-3.

In the said circumstances benefit of doubt is extended to A-2 and A-3.
9.
In the result Crl.A.No.376 of 2010 is dismissed and Crl.A.No.234 of 2009 and Crl.A.No208 of 2009 are allowed.
The trial Court shall cause appearance of A-1 and send him to prison to serve out the remaining part of the sentence.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
